comment: oi_tkn_id and oi_au_id are OpenIddict's own token and authorization identifiers, the same ones accepted in the Basic plan: OpenIddict resolves the stored token from them, so they are not ours to drop, and they say nothing about the user.

The server offers the refresh_token grant, but the plan's clients do not ask for offline_access, so no refresh token is issued and the module skips. Refresh tokens have their own tests in RefreshTokenTests.

An expired request_uri is refused, but on the OP's own error page instead of as a redirect carrying invalid_request_uri. OpenIddict drops the request while extracting it, before any redirect URI has been resolved — the authorization request carries only client_id and request_uri — so there is nowhere to send the error. No authorization is granted and the user is told; sending the error to the client would mean recovering the redirect URI from the registration first. Tracked in docs/plans/PLAN-FAPI2-CONFORMANCE.md.
